question_text: Find the length of the intercepts made by the circle x² + y² + 4x − 6y − 5 = 0 on the coordinate axes.

mark_split.label: Read g, f, c and write both formulas

insider_note: The two formulas differ by one letter — g for the x-axis and f for the y-axis — and swapping them is the only way to lose this question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Read g, f, c and write both formulas
steps.margin_note: One mark. g goes with the x-intercept, f with the y-intercept. Both subtract c.
steps.memory_tip: x-intercept 2√(g² − c), y-intercept 2√(f² − c). The letter matches the axis.
steps.why: Putting y = 0 in the circle gives a quadratic in x whose two roots are where the circle cuts the x-axis, and the difference of those roots works out to 2√(g² − c). The same argument with x = 0 gives the y-intercept.
common_mistakes: Using f for the x-intercept and g for the y-intercept.

steps.label: Compute the two intercepts
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both values under the root are positive, so the circle really does cut both axes.
steps.memory_tip: 4 + 5 = 9 is a perfect square; 9 + 5 = 14 is not.
steps.why: Since c = −5, subtracting it adds 5 in both formulas. Both results are positive, which confirms the circle meets each axis at two points.
common_mistakes: Writing 2√14 as √28 and then simplifying wrongly.
Giving half the intercept by leaving out the factor 2.
